s0301.literal: Now the great forge pours form into the myriad things — who could name the merit of the primordial source?
s0301.idiomatic: Now the great forge pours form into every creature — who could name the primordial source's merit?

s0302.literal: I alone bring tranquillity to the myriad states, and am all the more intent on embodying benevolence.
s0302.idiomatic: I alone bring peace to every realm, and am all the more intent on embodying benevolence.

s0303.literal: Affairs follow what is inherited and what is changed; the Way accords heaven and man.
s0303.idiomatic: Government follows what is inherited and what must be changed; the Way keeps heaven and humanity in accord.

s0305.literal: Naming by what is right is assuredly not to heap excess praise upon it;
s0305.idiomatic: To name the dynasty by its rightful meaning is certainly not to lavish undue praise;

s0306.literal: Trust in blessings is everlasting — still not to fall short in the hardship one has undertaken.
s0306.idiomatic: May trust in blessings endure forever — and still not fall short in the hardship we have undertaken.

s0307.literal: Rejoice with all beneath heaven and together exalt the great designation.
s0307.idiomatic: Rejoice with all under heaven and together exalt the great dynastic name.

s0308.literal: On bingxu day, Sichuan Province was established at Chengdu.
s0308.idiomatic: On bingxu day Sichuan province was established at Chengdu.

s0309.literal: The Wanyan Pavilion at Shangdu was completed.
s0309.idiomatic: The Wanyan Pavilion at Shangdu was completed.

s0310.literal: On the xinmao new moon of the twelfth month, an edict ordered schools for the national script raised throughout the realm.
s0310.idiomatic: On the xinmao new moon of the twelfth month an edict ordered national-script schools established throughout the realm.

s0311.literal: The Palace Attendants Bureau requested that stray households, unregistered households, and the like be put to gold-panning; the Emperor said: "For now stop — do not overtax Our people again.
s0311.idiomatic: The palace attendants bureau asked to assign stray and unregistered households to gold-panning; the Emperor said, "Stop for now — do not burden Our people further.

s0312.literal: " On yisi day, officials' salaries were reduced.
s0312.idiomatic: " On yisi day officials' salaries were reduced.

s0313.idiomatic: Fields in Western Xia were surveyed.

s0314.literal: Tachu and Dong Wenbing were summoned to court.
s0314.idiomatic: Tachu and Dong Wenbing were summoned to court.

s0315.literal: On xinhai day, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was merged into the Hanlin Academy, and the Palace Repairs Directorate into the Directorate for Imperial Manufacturers.
s0315.idiomatic: On xinhai day the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was merged into the Hanlin Academy and the palace repairs directorate into the directorate for imperial manufacturers.

s0316.literal: On jiayin day, an edict ordered the Ministry of State transferred into the Central Secretariat.
s0316.idiomatic: On jiayin day an edict ordered the ministry of state moved into the Central Secretariat.

s0317.literal: That year, households under heaven numbered 1,946,270.

s0318.literal: Gold, silver, silk currency, and cloth were granted to the consorts of the previous reign and to the princes according to annual custom; 11,167 ingots of notes were granted to the Nangjia and others for sheep and horse prices.
s0318.idiomatic: Former consorts and the princes received gold, silver, notes, and cloth as in annual custom; the Nangjia and others were granted 11,167 ingots of notes for sheep and horse prices.

s0319.literal: One hundred five persons were sentenced to death.
s0319.idiomatic: One hundred five persons were sentenced to death.

s0320.literal: In the ninth year, spring, first month, on the gengshen new moon, King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo sent his minister, Rites Reception Director Xuan Wenie, to offer congratulations and also deliver the annual tribute.
s0320.idiomatic: In the ninth year, on the gengshen new moon of the first month of spring, King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo sent Rites Reception Director Xuan Wenie with congratulations and the annual tribute.

s0321.literal: On jiazi day, the Ministry of State was merged into the Central Secretariat; Ahmad, Equal-in-Rank Minister administering Ministry of State affairs, and Zhang Yi, Concurrent Equal-in-Rank Minister administering Ministry of State affairs, were both made Equal-in-Rank Grand Councillors of the Central Secretariat; Zhang Hui, Associate Administrator of Ministry of State affairs, was made Left Associate of the Central Secretariat; Li Yaozi and Maisuding, Associate Administrators of Ministry of State affairs, were both made Associate Administrators of Central Secretariat affairs.
s0321.idiomatic: On jiazi day the ministry of state was merged back into the Central Secretariat; Ahmad and Zhang Yi, equal-in-rank ministers of the ministry of state, were both made equal-in-rank grand councillors of the Central Secretariat; Zhang Hui became left associate of the Central Secretariat, and Li Yaozi and Maisuding became associate administrators of Central Secretariat affairs.

s0322.literal: The posts of supervising secretary, secretariat drafter, and reviewer were abolished; left and right sections were retained; the six ministries were reduced to four; and the designation was changed to Central Secretariat.
s0322.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries, secretariat drafters, and reviewers were abolished; left and right sections were kept; the six ministries were cut to four; and everything was renamed under the Central Secretariat.

s0323.literal: On bingyin day, an edict dispatched Buqa and Ma Lin to instruct Goryeo to furnish ships and grain to aid the campaign against Tamna.
s0323.idiomatic: On bingyin day an edict sent Buqa and Ma Lin to tell Goryeo to supply ships and grain for the Tamna campaign.

s0324.literal: Henan Province requested additional troops; an edict ordered thirty thousand soldiers levied from various routes.
s0324.idiomatic: Henan province asked for more troops; the court ordered thirty thousand men levied from the routes.

s0325.literal: On dingchou day, an edict ordered Prince Orluk of Xi Ping, Aruq Temür, Töge, and the forces under Prince Tulu of Nan Ping, together with the Sichuan branch secretariat forces under Yesu Dai'er, the eighteen tribes of Mangudai, and the Tibetan troops of Yisuqongnong and others, to campaign jointly against Jiandu.
s0325.idiomatic: On dingchou day an edict ordered Prince Orluk of Xi Ping, Aruq Temür, Töge, and Prince Tulu of Nan Ping, together with Yesu Dai'er's Sichuan branch secretariat command, Mangudai's eighteen tribes, and the Tibetan troops under Yisuqongnong, to campaign jointly against Jiandu.

s0326.literal: Xin'an Prefecture had originally been subordinate to Xiong Prefecture; an edict made it a county under Shuntian.
s0326.idiomatic: Xin'an Prefecture, formerly subordinate to Xiong Prefecture, was made a county under Shuntian.

s0327.literal: On gengchen day, the branch ministries of state at the Beijing, Zhongxing, Sichuan, and Henan routes were changed to branch secretariats.
s0327.idiomatic: On gengchen day branch ministries at the Beijing, Zhongxing, Sichuan, and Henan routes were renamed branch secretariats.

s0328.literal: Jingzhao again established a branch secretariat and also ordered Prince Jibiytemür to set up adjudication officers for the secretariat.
s0328.idiomatic: A branch secretariat was reestablished at Jingzhao and Prince Jibiytemür was ordered to appoint secretariat adjudication officers.

s0329.literal: Horse-price bows and arrows were granted to Prince Orluk of Xi Ping; Prince Tulu of Nan Ping was granted five silver seals and five each of gold and silver tallies.
s0329.idiomatic: Prince Orluk of Xi Ping received bows and arrows paid for at horse price; Prince Tulu of Nan Ping was granted five silver seals and five each of gold and silver tallies.

s0330.literal: On xinsi day, garrison-farming at Feng Prefecture was transferred to Yan and Bai prefectures.
s0330.idiomatic: On xinsi day garrison-farming at Feng Prefecture was moved to Yan and Bai prefectures.

s0331.literal: An edict ordered Dong Wenbing to patrol and raid the southern frontier from time to time and not let the Song erect fortresses.
s0331.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dong Wenbing to patrol and raid the south periodically so the Song could not establish fortresses.

s0332.literal: An edict stated: "Where military and civilian households dispute fields, if civilian fields are surplus they shall be divided to the military; if military fields are surplus they shall likewise be divided to the civilians.
s0332.idiomatic: An edict stated, "In land disputes between military and civilian households, surplus civilian land goes to soldiers and surplus military land to civilians.

s0333.literal: Capable officials are still to be sent to assess fair value; soldier-slaves entered into civilian registers shall be restored to their proper status.
s0333.idiomatic: Competent officials were still to assess fair purchase prices, and soldier-slaves wrongly entered in civilian registers were to be restored.

s0334.literal: " An edict ordered the Prince of Yan to dispatch envoys bearing incense banners to sacrifice at the mountains and rivers, Earth Lord, and Xingguo Temple on Wutai.
s0334.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the Prince of Yan to send envoys with incense banners to sacrifice at the mountains and rivers, Earth Lord, and Xingguo Temple on Wutai.

s0335.literal: Liu Zheng was ordered to command the Han armies.
s0335.idiomatic: Liu Zheng was placed in overall command of the Han armies.

s0336.literal: On renwu day, the grand marshal's headquarters and army command of eastern Shandong route were changed to a branch privy council; Yesu Dai'er and Tachu were both made deputy commissioners of the branch privy council.
s0336.idiomatic: On renwu day the eastern Shandong route grand marshal's army command was converted into a branch privy council; Yesu Dai'er and Tachu were both made its deputy commissioners.

s0337.literal: On yiyou day, the ritual for officials receiving imperial patents and edicts was fixed.
s0337.idiomatic: On yiyou day the ceremony for officials receiving imperial patents and edicts was fixed.

s0338.literal: An edict ordered grand marshal headquarters, army commands, and wanhu headquarters to verify military registers.
s0338.idiomatic: An edict ordered grand marshals' headquarters, army commands, and wanhu commands to verify military registers.

s0339.literal: Second month, on the gengyin new moon, Zhao Liangbi, envoy to Japan, sent document clerk Zhang Tuo together with twenty-six Japanese to the capital seeking audience.
s0339.idiomatic: On the gengyin new moon of the second month Zhao Liangbi, envoy to Japan, sent document clerk Zhang Tuo with twenty-six Japanese to the capital seeking audience.

s0340.literal: On xinmao day, an edict stated: "The jarquchi was established at the very founding by Taizu and ranks to the right of all offices; let him be granted a silver seal and establish left and right sections.
s0340.idiomatic: On xinmao day an edict stated, "The jarquchi post was created at Taizu's founding and ranks above all offices; grant it a silver seal and establish left and right sections.

s0341.literal: " On renchen day, King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo sent his minister, Marquis of Qi'an Wang Shu, to congratulate the change of dynastic name.
s0341.idiomatic: " On renchen day King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo sent Qi'an Marquis Wang Shu to congratulate the change of dynastic name.

s0342.literal: Central Capital was changed to Great Capital.
s0342.idiomatic: Central Capital was renamed Great Capital (Dadu).

s0343.literal: On jiawu day, Aju was ordered to command the Mongol armies; Liu Zheng and Ariq Haiya were ordered to command the Han armies.
s0343.idiomatic: On jiawu day Aju was placed in command of the Mongol armies and Liu Zheng and Ariq Haiya of the Han armies.

s0344.literal: On wuxu day, because Dongping and Western Capital prefectures and counties had suffered drought, locusts, and floods the previous year, their rents and levies were remitted.
s0344.idiomatic: On wuxu day rents and levies were remitted in Dongping and Western Capital prefectures and counties afflicted the previous year by drought, locusts, and flooding.

s0345.literal: On gengzi day, Biyang County in Tang Prefecture was restored.
s0345.idiomatic: On gengzi day Biyang County in Tang Prefecture was restored.

s0346.literal: The Central Secretariat office was built at Dadu.
s0346.idiomatic: A Central Secretariat office was built at Dadu.

s0347.literal: On wushen day, sacrifice to the First Farmer began with the same rites as sacrifice to the Earth Altar.
s0347.idiomatic: On wushen day sacrifice to the First Farmer began, using the same rites as the Earth Altar.

s0348.literal: An edict ordered waterways dredged and opened in all routes.
s0348.idiomatic: An edict ordered waterways dredged throughout the routes.

s0349.literal: The imperial carriage proceeded to Shangdu.

s0350.literal: Third month, on yichou day, an instruction was issued to the Central Secretariat that the Japanese envoys should be quickly discussed and sent back.
s0350.idiomatic: In the third month, on yichou day, the Central Secretariat was instructed to decide quickly on sending the Japanese envoys home.

s0351.literal: Antong said: "Liangbi requests transferring the garrison at Jin Prefecture so Japan will not groundlessly give rise to suspicion and fear.
s0351.idiomatic: Antong said, "Zhao Liangbi asks to transfer the Jin Prefecture garrison so Japan does not take needless alarm.

s0352.literal: We your ministers consider that the Jin Prefecture garrison is known to that country; if the garrison is moved again, I fear it would not be suitable.
s0352.idiomatic: We think the Jin Prefecture garrison is known to them; moving it again would probably be unwise.

s0353.literal: Only openly instruct the envoys who have come that this garrison was temporarily established for Tamna; you need not suspect and fear.
s0353.idiomatic: Only explain openly to the envoys that this garrison was set up temporarily for Tamna, and that they need not fear.

s0355.literal: On jiaxu day, the Four Teachings Scripture among the people was collected and burned.
s0355.idiomatic: On jiaxu day copies of the Four Teachings Scripture among the people were seized and burned.

s0356.literal: Grand Marshal Aju of the Mongol armies, and Grand Marshals Liu Zheng and Ariq Haiya of the Han armies, supervised their forces in breaking the outer wall of Fan, beheading two thousand, capturing sixteen officers alive, and building up a heavier encirclement to hold it.
s0356.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Aju of the Mongol armies and Grand Marshals Liu Zheng and Ariq Haiya of the Han armies led their forces in breaching Fan's outer wall, killing two thousand, capturing sixteen officers, and tightening the siege.

s0357.literal: Famine relief was given in Jinan Route.
s0357.idiomatic: Famine relief was sent to Jinan route.

s0358.literal: An edict remitted corvée and miscellany for physician households.
s0358.idiomatic: An edict exempted physician households from corvée and miscellaneous levies.

s0359.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jichou day, an edict ordered Ninghe Post established on the border between Tibetan and western Chuan territories.
s0359.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on jichou day, an edict ordered Ninghe Post set up on the Tibetan-western Chuan border.

s0360.literal: On xinmao day, horses were granted to the command of Prince Aiyachi.
s0360.idiomatic: On xinmao day horses were granted to Prince Aiyachi's command.

s0361.literal: On bingwu day, grain was issued to the command of Prince Orluk of Xi Ping.
s0361.idiomatic: On bingwu day grain was issued to Prince Orluk of Xi Ping's command.

s0362.literal: On jiayin day, famine relief was given in Dadu Route.
s0362.idiomatic: On jiayin day famine relief was sent to Dadu route.

s0363.literal: Fifth month, on the wuwu new moon, the Karakorum Transport Commission was established, with Xiao Yunshibie as commissioner, concurrently superintendent of note circulation.
s0363.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon of the fifth month the Karakorum transport commission was established, with Xiao Yunshibie as commissioner and concurrent superintendent of note circulation.

s0364.literal: On jiwei day, two silver tallies for sea-hawks were granted to Kököchü.
s0364.idiomatic: On jiwei day Kököchü received two silver tallies for hunting hawks.

s0365.literal: On xinyou day, the levy of Hui troops was abolished.
s0365.idiomatic: On xinyou day the draft of Hui troops was abolished.

s0366.literal: On guihai day, an edict ordered Batu's army to open canals and plow fields at Qielunan.
s0366.idiomatic: On guihai day an edict ordered Batu's army to dig canals and farm at Qielunan.

s0367.literal: On bingyin day, ten thousand able-bodied men from Xu and Pi prefectures were levied to garrison Pi Prefecture.
s0367.idiomatic: On bingyin day ten thousand able-bodied men from Xu and Pi prefectures were levied to garrison Pi Prefecture.

s0368.literal: On gengwu day, iron-smelting households were reduced; gold and silver mining households at Tibetan Tulugan and elsewhere were abolished and made civilians.
s0368.idiomatic: On gengwu day iron-smelting households were reduced, and gold and silver mining households in Tibetan Tulugan and elsewhere were abolished and returned to civilian status.

s0369.literal: Han people gathering in crowds to brawl with Mongols were forbidden.
s0369.idiomatic: Han crowds brawling with Mongols were forbidden.

s0370.literal: An edict ordered deliberation on taking Tamna and Jeju.
s0370.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation on seizing Tamna and Jeju.

s0371.literal: On xinsi day, an edict ordered the capital walls built; all costs were to be paid entirely from official funds, nothing taken from the people, and the tax levies of woodcutting laborers were also remitted.
s0371.idiomatic: On xinsi day an edict ordered construction of the capital walls at full official expense with no levies on the people, and taxes on woodcutting laborers were remitted.

s0372.literal: On jiashen day, an edict addressed soldier-household attendants in all routes: except those who before the seventh year of the Zhiyuan era had obtained freedom and entered civilian registers and thus owed corvée, though the rest had obtained freedom, all were ordered to assist their original households' military service.
s0372.idiomatic: On jiashen day an edict addressed soldier-household attendants in all routes: only those freed and entered in civilian registers before Zhiyuan 7 owed corvée; the rest, though freed, still had to assist their original households' military service.

s0373.literal: On yiyou day, Venus encroached on the star at the spacing of Bi.
s0373.idiomatic: On yiyou day Venus passed the spacing star of Bi.

s0374.literal: The palace city first built the Eastern and Western Hua gates and the Left and Right Flanking gates.
s0374.idiomatic: The palace city first built the Eastern and Western Hua gates and the Left and Right Flanking gates.

s0375.literal: An edict ordered settlement of the displaced people under Darib.
s0375.idiomatic: An edict ordered the resettlement of displaced people under Darib.

s0376.literal: Sixth month, on renchen day, the various darughachis of Goryeo's Western Capital and dependent cities and hostages such as Jin Yi were sent home to their country.
s0376.idiomatic: On renchen day of the sixth month the darughachis of Goryeo's Western Capital and its dependent cities, with hostages including Jin Yi, were sent home.

s0377.literal: Rents from the garrison farm at Qirghiz were reduced; one hundred southerners were still dispatched, furnished with oxen and tools, to go there.
s0377.idiomatic: Rents from the Qirghiz garrison farm were reduced, and one hundred southerners were sent with oxen and tools.

s0378.literal: That night, heavy rain in the capital destroyed walls and houses; many were crushed to death.
s0378.idiomatic: That night a great storm in the capital destroyed walls and houses and killed many.

s0379.literal: On guisi day, an edict used grain stored from the ceremonial field to relieve the people; when insufficient, nearby official granaries were also opened to aid them.
s0379.idiomatic: On guisi day grain from the ceremonial field stores was issued for relief; when that proved insufficient nearby official granaries were opened as well.

s0380.literal: On jiawu day, Goryeo reported famine; twenty thousand shi of grain from Dongjing were transferred to relieve it.
s0380.idiomatic: On jiawu day Goryeo reported famine, and twenty thousand shi of Dongjing grain was sent for relief.

s0381.literal: On jihai day, Tachu of the eastern Shandong branch privy council, on the thirteenth day of the fourth month, sent infantry and cavalry toward Lian Prefecture, captured four fortresses at Shelonggou, Wugangkou, the salt works, and Baitou River, killed more than three hundred Song troops, captured people and cattle to the number of ten thousand, and graded merits and rewards in varying amounts.
s0381.idiomatic: On jihai day Tachu of the eastern Shandong branch privy council reported that on the thirteenth of the fourth month he had sent infantry and cavalry toward Lian Prefecture, taken four fortresses at Shelonggou, Wugangkou, the salt works, and Baitou River, killed more than three hundred Song troops, captured people and cattle by the ten thousand, and graded rewards accordingly.

s0382.literal: On xinhai day, King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo requested to campaign against the remaining Tamna bandits.
s0382.idiomatic: On xinhai day King Wang Chŏn of Goryeo asked to campaign against remaining Tamna bandits.

s0383.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on the dingji new moon, Henan provincial officials said: "In previous years people were relocated to garrison and farm the frontier borders; because of hardship they all dispersed and returned home.
s0383.idiomatic: On the dingji new moon of the seventh month Henan provincial officials said, "Frontier resettlement and garrison farming had sent people back home in poverty.

s0384.literal: Now the people of Tang, Deng, Cai, Xi, Xu, and Pi love their fields and homes, still hold their old garrisons, and wish to deliver grain by conversion at silk and silver rates; yet the inland prefectures and counties that transport grain to supply the army find it on the contrary irksome.
s0384.idiomatic: People in Tang, Deng, Cai, Xi, Xu, and Pi preferred their own fields, stayed at their old garrison farms, and offered to pay grain levies in silk or silver; inland prefectures and counties supplying troops by grain transport found the burden heavy.

s0385.literal: Your ministers propose that this year the frontier prefectures and commanderies should continue their old grain deliveries; inland prefectures and commanderies, according to their household numbers, should let them convert to notes and purchase grain along the frontier — thus both sides would find it mutually convenient.
s0385.idiomatic: We propose that frontier prefectures keep delivering grain as before, while inland prefectures, by household count, pay notes to buy grain on the frontier — easing the burden on both sides.

s0387.literal: " Unregistered households in the Kaiyuan, Dongjing, and other routes were rounded up and registered.
s0387.idiomatic: " Unregistered households in Kaiyuan, Dongjing, and other routes were rounded up and registered.

s0388.literal: Private sale of the Hui calendar was forbidden.
s0388.idiomatic: Private sale of the Hui calendar was forbidden.

s0389.literal: Famine relief was given to the Udaid tribe.
s0389.idiomatic: Famine relief was sent to the Udaid tribe.

s0390.literal: On wuyin day, paper notes were granted to the princes of the Babu tribe.
s0390.idiomatic: On wuyin day the princes of the Babu tribe received paper notes.

s0391.literal: Monks in the capital were assembled to recite the Great Canon in nine sessions.
s0391.idiomatic: Monks in the capital were assembled for nine sessions of reciting the Great Canon.

s0392.literal: On renwu day, Huluhuosun memorialized: "Schools for the Mongol script have been established in the national academy, yet children of Han officials still have no students enrolled; and in government documents there are still Uighur characters.
s0392.idiomatic: On renwu day Huluhuosun memorialized, "National-script schools exist, but Han officials' sons are not enrolling, and government documents still use Uighur script.

s0393.literal: " An edict ordered that henceforth all edicts and orders use the Mongol script exclusively, and officials' sons were still sent to enroll in the schools.
s0393.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that henceforth all edicts use the Mongol script exclusively and that officials' sons be sent to school.

s0394.literal: On yiyou day, relocation of Daluo Fort residents was remitted; they were ordered to deliver double rent-grain to the hawk offices.
s0394.idiomatic: On yiyou day relocation of residents from Daluo Fort was canceled; they were ordered to pay double rent-grain to the hawk offices instead.

s0395.literal: An edict ordered separate review of tammaqchi slave households' registers in Dadu, Jingzhao, and elsewhere.
s0395.idiomatic: An edict ordered a separate review of tammaqchi slave-household registers in Dadu, Jingzhao, and elsewhere.

s0396.literal: Eighth month, on the bingxu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
s0396.idiomatic: On the bingxu new moon of the eighth month there was a solar eclipse.

s0397.literal: On wuzi day, the Herd Directorate was established, managing pasture horses and imperial saddles and bridles.
s0397.idiomatic: On wuzi day the herd directorate was established to manage pasture horses and imperial saddlery.

s0398.literal: On renchen day, an edict ordered Mangan Granary and Jing Prefecture to store fifty thousand shi of grain in advance to supply provisions to newly relocated Hongjila tribespeople and westerners who had submitted inward.
s0398.idiomatic: On renchen day an edict ordered fifty thousand shi stored in advance at Mangan Granary and Jing Prefecture to feed newly relocated Hongjila tribespeople and newly submitted westerners.

s0399.literal: Troops were transferred to reinforce the garrison at Jeonla Prefecture.
s0399.idiomatic: Troops were redeployed to reinforce the garrison at Jeonla.

s0400.literal: On yiwei day, all persons who on their own affairs presumptuously called out the supreme honorific title were forbidden.
s0400.idiomatic: On yiwei day it was forbidden to use the supreme imperial title in private disputes.
